answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making trust grow like a juniper on karst: slow, rooted, and hard to fake. New identities start with a tiny spending cap, and the cap only rises after they complete verified work — each finished job leaves a quartz-clear, on-chain receipt anyone can audit. An attacker could spin up thousands of fresh identities, but each would sit at the bottom of the cap, unable to move meaningful value until it had done real, checkable work over weeks. Faking volume then costs more in time and effort than it earns, so the cheap-identity attack collapses.
